claims.quotedLanguage: The City of Eagle Water Department provides water services to approximately 3,800 households within the City of Eagle. ... In separately designated areas of Eagle, residents may receive water services from Veolia (FKA SUEZ).
claims.notes: The practical point: two Eagle neighbours can be on different water utilities, with different billing and different rules. ⚠️ Never infer which utility serves an address from a neighbourhood name; the city lists subdivisions, and federal records also show a private Dry Creek Water Company and a separate Avimor system whose areas were not mapped. ⚠️ Veolia's former Eagle Water Company customers sit on their own rate schedule — see eagle-veolia-acquired-eagle-water-company.

claims.claim: The City of Eagle identifies two sources of flooding in the city, Dry Creek and the Boise River. The city participates in the National Flood Insurance Program, which makes federally backed flood insurance available to property owners and tenants, and it publishes elevation certificates searchable by address.
claims.quotedLanguage: Flooding in our city may be caused by two sources; Dry Creek and the Boise River.
claims.notes: Useful because owners watch the river and forget the creek. ⚠️ The same page quotes a FloodSmart.gov statistic on flood risk over a 30-year mortgage; it is the federal program's figure, not the city's, and is not claimed here. ⚠️ Whether a specific parcel is in a mapped flood hazard area is not inferred from either source's name.

claims.claim: Kuna's drinking water comes from wells owned and operated by the City of Kuna. Federal records list the Kuna city system as owned by local government and supplied by groundwater, serving 32,038 people through 11,363 connections.
claims.quotedLanguage: The City of Kuna owns and operates several wells that provide potable drinking water to Kuna residents.
claims.notes: Contrast worth making on the page: in Boise drinking water comes from private Commission-regulated utilities, while in Kuna the city itself runs the wells. ⚠️ The city describes its system as one of the newest in the state; that is the city's own characterisation and is not claimed as a fact. ⚠️ Commission records also list two very small regulated water companies with Kuna as their nearest town; their service areas were not mapped, so 'the city serves Kuna' must not become 'the city serves every Kuna parcel'.

claims.claim: Kuna requires a residential building permit for, among other things, a new residence, mobile home or accessory dwelling unit; accessory structures such as garages or residential storage structures, though detached storage buildings under 200 square feet are exempt; improvements and additions to existing residences or accessory structures; decks over 30 inches above grade; retaining walls over 4 feet including footing; the installation of fences; heating, air-conditioning, fireplaces, wood stoves and ventilation systems; and relocating or demolishing a structure.
claims.quotedLanguage: Detached storage buildings less than 200 square feet in area are exempt
claims.notes: ⚠️ Kuna lists 'installation of fences' without a height threshold, where Star requires a permit only for fences over 6 feet. Kuna's own list is quoted; do not add a height exemption Kuna does not state, and never carry either city's rule to the other. Seller relevance is unpermitted work surfacing at inspection.

claims.claim: Garden City's public water system is the Garden City Water and Sewer System, which federal records list as owned by local government and supplied by groundwater, serving 12,500 people through 4,595 connections.
claims.quotedLanguage: GARDEN CITY WATER AND SEWER SYSTEM
claims.notes: ⚠️ Sourced to the federal record only — the city's own water page was not read. Ownership is EPA's owner-type code, which is reliable for a municipal system but should be confirmed against the city before anything more specific is said. ⚠️ Federal records also list small private mobile home park systems with Garden City addresses.

claims.claim: In Garden City's Special Flood Hazard Area, any reconstruction, rehabilitation, addition or other improvement to a building equal to or exceeding 50 percent of the building's value must meet the same standards as new development. A city floodplain application is also required before working in the floodplain or floodway, before removing or damaging vegetation within 25 feet of the river or on the riverside of the greenbelt or nature path, and to request a Letter of Map Change.
claims.quotedLanguage: any reconstruction, rehabilitation, addition or other improvements to a building that equal or exceed 50% of the building’s value, must comply with the same standards as any new development in the SFHA
claims.notes: 🎯 One of the most seller-relevant facts on any place page: a buyer planning a large renovation of a house in Garden City's flood hazard area may have to bring the whole building up to new-construction flood standards, which changes what that buyer can pay. ⚠️ How the city calculates 'the building's value' is not stated on the page read; never compute the threshold for a reader.

claims.claim: In Garden City the uses allowed in each zoning district are set out in Garden City Code Table 8-2B-1, some uses carry further conditions under Code 8-2C, and a property may also sit within the Neighborhood Commercial Node (NCN) overlay district, whose allowed uses are in Table 8-3A-1.
claims.quotedLanguage: Garden City Code Table 8-2B-1 shows what uses are allowed in a specific zoning district.
claims.notes: ⚠️ Names the tables; does not claim what any of them permits. Garden City's C-2 district is mixed use, unlike the C-2 districts of neighbouring cities — see the commercial registry — so district letters must never be read across city limits.

claims.claim: Meridian's municipal drinking water is supplied by the City of Meridian's Water Division from 25 large-capacity groundwater wells, between 400 and 800 feet deep, drawing on the Snake River Plain Aquifer System. Federal records list the Meridian system as supplied by groundwater, serving 147,340 people through 47,953 connections.
claims.quotedLanguage: The City of Meridian gets its water from the Snake River Plain Aquifer System flowing underneath the City. ... Water is accessed through 25 large capacity, deep (between 400 and 800 feet) groundwater wells throughout the City.
claims.notes: Contrast with Boise, where drinking water comes from private Commission-regulated utilities. ⚠️ EPA's owner_type_code for this system is P; the city's own Water Division pages say the city runs it, and the owner type is deliberately not asserted. ⚠️ EPA's population served exceeds the city's population estimate, so the system's reach and the city limits are not the same thing; 'the city serves every Meridian parcel' is not claimed.

claims.claim: When a Meridian property is sold or refinanced, the agency handling the transaction must request a final billing option from the City of Meridian's Utility Billing office so the city can provide a final assessment for the property at the time of ownership transfer.
claims.quotedLanguage: These requests are required in order to provide a final assessment for the property in question at the time of ownership transfer.
claims.notes: The request is made by the title, mortgage or finance company handling the sale. The page does not state a deadline or a fee for the request, and none is claimed.

claims.claim: City of Meridian utility accounts stay with the property rather than travelling with the customer, any debt at the property for city services is the property owner's responsibility regardless of who used the services, and the account number changes when the property is sold to another owner.
claims.quotedLanguage: City accounts do not travel with the customer; they stay with the property. ... Any debt at the property regarding City services is the responsibility of the property owner regardless of ... If the property is sold to another owner
claims.notes: Stated on the city's rental-properties billing page, but the ownership rule is general: it is what makes a landlord liable for a tenant's unpaid city utility balance. Optional third-party (tenant) billing requires a Renters Addendum and a Billing Directive and carries a one-time $20.00 charge; the landlord still receives delinquent notices.

claims.claim: The City of Meridian does not control any surface (ditch) water supplies. Most Meridian subdivisions have pressurized irrigation systems along the back-lot lines, mostly fed by surface water that is not safe to drink, and those systems are not owned or operated by the city.
claims.quotedLanguage: The City of Meridian does not control any surface water (ditch water) supplies. ... Pressurized irrigation systems are not owned or operated by the City of Meridian.
claims.notes: The city directs owners to their homeowners association or an online map to find who runs a given system, and lists eight irrigation entities including Settlers, Nampa & Meridian, Boise-Kuna, New York and Pioneer. Which entity serves a particular parcel is not claimed.

claims.claim: The City of Meridian's water and sewer fee schedule effective March 5, 2025 sets a water base fee of $5.94, a water usage charge of $2.06 per 1,000 gallons, a sewer base fee of $9.35, a sewer usage charge of $5.99 per 1,000 gallons and a water turn-on charge of $32.00.
claims.quotedLanguage: Effective March 5, 2025 Water and Sewer Fee Schedule ... Water Base Fee $5.94 ... Water Usage Charge (per 1,000 gallons) $2.06 ... Sewer Base Fee $9.35 ... Sewer Usage Charge (per 1,000 gallons) $5.99 ... Water Turn-On Charge $32.00
claims.notes: ⚠️ Rates change; always state the effective date alongside the figures. The page does not state the base-fee billing period beyond 'monthly bills', and no annual total is computed or claimed.

claims.claim: In Meridian a homeowner or business owner is responsible for maintaining and repairing a portion of the water and sewer lines that run from the property to the street. The city maintains the lines in the public right of way; if a problem is on the owner's side of the property line, the owner must hire a plumber.
claims.quotedLanguage: As a homeowner or business owner, you are responsible for the maintenance and repair of a portion of the water and sewer lines that run from your property to the street. ... If the issue is on the owner's side of the property line, the property owner will need to call a plumbing company for assistance.
claims.notes: ⚠️ The city also says neither Digline nor the city can locate lines on private property — an 811 call marks lines in easements and streets only. Where exactly the owner's portion ends on a given lot is not claimed.

claims.claim: Meridian's wastewater is treated by the City of Meridian at its Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility, while the city directs stormwater questions to the Ada County Highway District.
claims.quotedLanguage: That is where Meridian's Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility (WRRF) comes into play. ... For information about stormwater, please contact ACHD at (208) 387-6100
claims.notes: Facility location on the city page: 3401 N. Ten Mile Road. That every Meridian parcel is on city sewer is not claimed.

claims.claim: For Idaho's property condition disclosure act, residential real property means real property improved by a building or structure with one to four dwelling units, or an individually owned unit in a structure of any size, and the term also covers real property with a combined residential and commercial use.
claims.quotedLanguage: "Residential real property" means real property that is improved by a building or other structure that has one (1) to four (4) dwelling units or an individually owned unit in a structure of any size. This also applies to real property which has a combined residential and commercial use.
claims.notes: An individually owned unit in a building of any size (a condominium) is covered; a building of five or more units sold whole is outside this definition. ⚠️ This is the disclosure act's definition only — never generalise it into 'five units is legally commercial'.

claims.claim: Idaho's disclosure requirement applies to transfers of one-to-four-unit residential property by sale, exchange, installment sale contract, lease with an option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements, unless the transfer is exempt.
claims.quotedLanguage: this chapter applies to any transfer by sale, exchange, installment sale contract, a lease with an option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements
claims.notes: Shows seller-financed and lease-option deals are covered, not only conventional sales.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 55-2505 lists sixteen kinds of transfer exempt from the disclosure requirement, including transfers to a buyer who has occupied the property as a personal residence for a year or more, transfers of inherited property by a seller who has not lived there within the prior year, transfers between co-owners, transfers to a spouse or lineal relatives, government transfers, uninhabited new construction, relocation-company transfers within a year, and transfers from a decedent's estate. None of the sixteen turns on the property being sold as-is.
claims.quotedLanguage: (8) A transfer from one (1) co-owner to one (1) or more other co-owners; (9) A transfer made to the transferor's spouse or to one (1) or more persons in the lineal line of consanguinity of one (1) or more of the transferors; ... (13) A transfer to a transferee who has occupied the property as a personal residence for one (1) or more years immediately prior to the transfer; (14) A transfer from a transferor who both has not occupied the property as a personal residence within one (1) year immediately prior to the transfer and has acquired the property through inheritance or devise; ... (16) A transfer from a decedent's estate.
claims.notes: 'None turns on as-is' is a reading of the complete sixteen-item list (all sixteen read on 2026-09-13), not a quotation — there is no as-is, repair-condition or cash-sale exemption. Exemption (13) matters for a tenant buying the home they have lived in; (14) needs BOTH conditions (inherited AND not occupied within a year).

claims.claim: Uninhabited newly constructed residential property is exempt from Idaho's disclosure form, except that its sellers must still disclose annexation and city-service status.
claims.quotedLanguage: A transfer that involved newly constructed residential real property that previously has not been inhabited, except that disclosure of annexation and city service status shall be declared by the sellers of such newly constructed residential real property
claims.notes: The statutory form's three questions ask whether the property is in an area of city impact subject to annexation, receives city services outside city limits, or has a recorded consent to annex.

claims.claim: Idaho's disclosure form must let the seller disclose material matters about the property's physical condition, including the source of water supply, the nature of the sewer system, the condition of the structure including roof, foundation, walls and floors, and the known presence of hazardous materials or substances.
claims.quotedLanguage: the source of water supply to the property; the nature of the sewer system serving the property; the condition of the structure of the property including the roof, foundation, walls and floors; the known presence of hazardous materials or substances
claims.notes: Alternative forms are allowed if they carry the same information and the mandatory statements in 55-2507.

claims.claim: An Idaho disclosure form must state that it records conditions and information actually known by the seller, that it is not a warranty of any kind by the seller or the seller's agent, and that it is not a substitute for any inspections.
claims.quotedLanguage: (1) The form constitutes a statement of the conditions of the property and of information concerning the property actually known by the transferor. ... (3) That the statement is not a warranty of any kind by the transferor or by any agent or subsequent agent representing the transferor in this transaction. (4) That the statement is not a substitute for any inspections.

claims.claim: An Idaho seller must deliver a signed and dated copy of the completed disclosure form to each prospective buyer or the buyer's agent within ten days of accepting the buyer's offer, and the buyer acknowledges receipt by signing, dating and returning a copy.
claims.quotedLanguage: Every transferor shall deliver, in accordance with section 55-2510, Idaho Code, a signed and dated copy of the completed disclosure form to each prospective transferee or his agent within ten (10) days of transferor's acceptance of transferee's offer.
claims.notes: The statute says ten (10) days without specifying business days. Do not add 'business'.

claims.claim: An Idaho seller and the seller's agents are not liable for an error, inaccuracy or omission in disclosed information that was not within the seller's personal knowledge, or that was based on information timely provided by public agencies or hired inspectors and obtained and passed on with ordinary care.
claims.quotedLanguage: Neither the transferor or transferor's agents shall be liable for any error, inaccuracy or omission of any information delivered pursuant to this chapter if the error, inaccuracy or omission was not within the personal knowledge of the transferor
claims.notes: ⚠️ Never present this as 'sellers are not liable'. It protects only what was outside personal knowledge or properly relied on; 55-2514 preserves other statutory and common-law duties. Not legal advice.

claims.claim: Under Idaho's disclosure act, information that becomes inaccurate because of something that happens after the disclosures are delivered is not a violation, and an item the seller cannot know may be given as an approximation if it is clearly identified as one, reasonable, based on the best information available and not used to evade the chapter.
claims.quotedLanguage: If information disclosed in accordance with this chapter is subsequently rendered inaccurate as a result of any act, occurrence or agreement subsequent to the delivery of the required disclosures, the inaccuracy resulting therefrom does not constitute a violation of this chapter.
claims.notes: The approximation route is conditioned on the seller's agent having made a reasonable effort to ascertain the item.

claims.claim: An Idaho seller must amend the disclosure statement before closing on discovering that information in it has changed, and a buyer's right to rescind after an amendment is strictly limited to the amendments.
claims.quotedLanguage: Transferor shall amend the disclosure statement prior to closing if transferor discovers any of the (the) information on the original statement has changed. In the event of amendments to the statement, transferee's right to rescind is strictly limited to the amendments to the disclosure statement.
claims.notes: '(the)' is a doubled word in the statute itself and is quoted as printed.

claims.claim: Idaho's disclosure act does not limit any obligation to disclose information that arises under any other section of the Idaho Code or under Idaho common law.
claims.quotedLanguage: does not limit and shall not be construed as limiting any obligation to disclose an item of information that is created by any other section of the Idaho Code or the common law of the state of Idaho
claims.notes: The reason an exemption from the FORM is never an exemption from honesty.

claims.claim: Every disclosure under Idaho's disclosure act must be made in good faith, which the act defines as honesty in fact in the conduct of the transaction.
claims.quotedLanguage: Each disclosure required in this chapter and each act which may be performed in making the disclosure shall be made in good faith. For the purposes of this chapter, good faith means honesty in fact, in the conduct of the transaction.

claims.claim: A failure to comply with Idaho's disclosure act does not by itself invalidate a transfer, but a person who willfully or negligently violates or fails to perform its duties is liable for the buyer's actual damages.
claims.quotedLanguage: No transfer, subject to this chapter, shall be invalidated solely because of the failure of any person to comply with any provision of this chapter. However, any person who willfully or negligently violates or fails to perform any duties prescribed by any provision of this chapter shall be liable in the amount of actual damages suffered by the transferee.
claims.notes: Not legal advice; the measure of damages in a given case is for counsel.

claims.claim: Under Idaho law no cause of action arises against an owner or the owner's representative for failing to disclose that real property is psychologically impacted — defined to include a suspected or actual suicide, homicide or felony at the property that had no effect on its physical condition, an occupant's non-transmissible disease, and a registered or suspected sex offender occupying or living near the property.
claims.quotedLanguage: No cause of action shall arise against an owner of real property or a representative of the owner for a failure to disclose to the transferee of the real property or a representative of the transferee that the real property was psychologically impacted. ... That the real property was at any time suspected of being the site of suicide, homicide or the commission of a felony which had no effect on the physical condition of the property or its environment or the structures located thereon
claims.notes: ⚠️ Limited to events with NO effect on physical condition. A felony that damaged the structure is not covered by this carve-out. amendmentHistory is 55-2802's; 55-2801 was redesignated by the same 2005 act.

claims.claim: If a buyer making a bona fide offer tells the owner's representative in writing that whether the property is psychologically impacted is important to the decision, the representative must ask the owner and, with the owner's consent and consistent with privacy law, report the findings; if the owner refuses, the buyer must be told the information will not be disclosed.
claims.quotedLanguage: If the owner refuses disclosure, the owner's representative shall advise the purchaser or the purchaser's representative that the information will not be disclosed.

claims.claim: For housing built before 1978, federal rules require the seller, before the buyer is obligated under the contract, to give the buyer an EPA-approved lead hazard pamphlet and disclose any known lead-based paint or lead-based paint hazards and any available records or reports; sales at foreclosure are excepted, as are housing for the elderly or persons with disabilities and 0-bedroom dwellings unless a child under six lives or is expected to live there.
claims.quotedLanguage: Target housing means any housing constructed prior to 1978, except housing for the elderly or persons with disabilities or any 0-bedroom dwelling ... The following activities shall be completed before the purchaser or lessee is obligated under any contract to purchase or lease target housing ... Sales of target housing at foreclosure.
claims.notes: Federal, applies in Idaho alongside the state form. 40 CFR 745.107 says nothing in the section obliges the seller to test or abate. No Idaho exemption (estate, inheritance, as-is) removes this federal duty — the only sale exception in 745.101 is foreclosure.

claims.claim: Before a buyer is obligated to purchase housing built before 1978, the seller must allow a 10-day period to conduct a lead-based paint risk assessment or inspection, unless the parties agree in writing on a different period; the buyer may waive the opportunity in writing.
claims.quotedLanguage: the seller shall permit the purchaser a 10-day period (unless the parties mutually agree, in writing, upon a different period of time) to conduct a risk assessment or inspection for the presence of lead-based paint and/or lead-based paint hazards

claims.claim: Idaho Code 32-903 makes a spouse's sole and separate property: property owned before marriage, property acquired afterward by gift, bequest, devise or descent, and property acquired with the proceeds of separate property.
claims.quotedLanguage: All property of either the husband or the wife owned by him or her before marriage, and that acquired afterward by either by gift, bequest, devise or descent, or that which either he or she shall acquire with the proceeds of his or her separate property, by way of moneys or other property, shall remain his or her sole and separate property.
claims.notes: ⚠️ State the categories as the statute lists them. Do NOT tell a reader that a house bought before marriage 'stays separate' as a conclusion about their facts: whether later payments, refinancing, a deed change or commingling affect character is a question this statute does not answer, and case law (not read here) does. Phrase as 'the statute lists' and send to an attorney.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 32-906(1), all other property acquired after marriage by either spouse — that is, property not within the separate-property categories of 32-903 — is community property, and the income of all property, separate or community, is community property unless the acquiring conveyance or a written agreement of both spouses provides otherwise.
claims.quotedLanguage: (1) All other property acquired after marriage by either husband or wife is community property. The income, including the rents, issues and profits, of all property, separate or community, is community property unless the conveyance by which it is acquired provides or both spouses, by written agreement specifically so providing, declare that all or specifically designated property and the income, including the rents, issues and profits, from all or the specifically designated property shall be the separate property of one of the spouses
claims.notes: ⚠️ 'All OTHER property' only makes sense read with 32-903; never quote the first sentence as 'everything acquired during marriage is community' without the 32-903 categories. ⚠️ The statute uses the words 'is community property'; it does not itself use the word 'presumption'. Do not write 'Idaho presumes' as if quoting this section. Income-from-separate-property rule is a real trap for a rental bought before marriage — state it, never apply it.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 32-906(2), property conveyed by one spouse to the other is presumed to be the grantee's sole and separate estate, and only the grantor spouse need sign and acknowledge that deed, notwithstanding 32-912; income from it is not the grantee's separate property unless the deed says so.
claims.quotedLanguage: (2) Property conveyed by one spouse to the other shall be presumed to be the sole and separate estate of the grantee and only the grantor spouse need execute and acknowledge the deed or other instrument of conveyance notwithstanding the provisions of section 32-912, Idaho Code; provided, however, that the income, including the rents, issues and profits, from such property shall not be the separate property of the grantee spouse unless this fact is specifically stated in the instrument of conveyance.
claims.notes: ⚠️ A PRESUMPTION, the statute's word. Never write that a quitclaim between spouses 'makes' the house separate property or is conclusive. Rebuttal is case law not read here.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 32-912, either spouse may manage and control community property, but neither may sell, convey or encumber community real estate unless the other joins in executing the sale agreement, deed or other instrument by which it is sold, conveyed or encumbered.
claims.quotedLanguage: Either the husband or the wife shall have the right to manage and control the community property, and either may bind the community property by contract, except that neither the husband nor wife may sell, convey or encumber the community real estate unless the other joins in executing the sale agreement, deed or other instrument of conveyance by which the real estate is sold, conveyed or encumbered,
claims.notes: ⚠️ Applies to COMMUNITY real estate. It covers the SALE AGREEMENT as well as the deed — the purchase contract, not only closing documents. Say nothing about what happens to a contract signed by one spouse alone (void/voidable is case law, not read). The statute does not address separate real property; 32-904 (not used) concerns a wife's separate property in old gendered language — do not cite it for a general rule.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 32-912 allows one spouse, by express power of attorney, to give the other complete power to sell, convey or encumber community property, real or personal.
claims.quotedLanguage: provided, however, that the husband or wife may by express power of attorney give to the other the complete power to sell, convey or encumber community property, either real or personal.
claims.notes: 'Express' power of attorney — do not imply a general or informal authority suffices. Whether a title company will accept a given POA is a title-company decision, not stated here.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 32-906A, community property that a married couple transfers to a revocable trust meeting the section's conditions remains community property during the marriage unless the trust expressly provides otherwise, and the section does not stop the trustee conveying trust property under the trust's terms without a spouse's consent unless the trust expressly requires it.
claims.quotedLanguage: the property so transferred to such trust, and the interests of the spouses in such trust, shall be community property during the continuance of the marriage, unless the trust otherwise expressly provides. ... nor shall this section be construed to prohibit the trustee from conveying any trust property, real or personal, in accordance with the provisions of the trust without the consent of the husband or wife unless the trust expressly required the consent of one or both spouses.
claims.amendmentHistory: [I.C., sec. 32-906A, as added by 1973, ch. 159, sec. 1, p. 304.]
claims.notes: ⚠️ Only for a trust meeting ALL THREE conditions (a)-(c) in the section (revocable during joint lives; provides property stays community; amendable on joint consent). Who signs for a trust-held house turns on the trust document — point to the trust and an attorney; never generalise.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 32-916 says spouses' property rights are governed by chapter 9 of Title 32 unless a marriage settlement agreement entered into during marriage contains contrary stipulations, and 32-917 requires marriage settlement contracts to be in writing and executed and acknowledged like conveyances of land.
claims.quotedLanguage: The property rights of husband and wife are governed by this chapter, unless there is a marriage settlement agreement entered into during marriage containing stipulations contrary thereto. ... All contracts for marriage settlements must be in writing, and executed and acknowledged or proved in like manner as conveyances of land are required to be executed and acknowledged or proved.
claims.notes: Two sections, two sources; quote joined with '...'. 32-916 as quoted refers to an agreement 'entered into during marriage'; premarital agreements (Uniform Premarital Agreement Act, 32-921 onward) were NOT read and must not be described from this claim.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 32-712 directs that on a divorce decree the court assigns community property in proportions it deems just, and that unless there are compelling reasons otherwise there shall be a substantially equal division in value, considering debts; it lists factors that may bear on whether the division is equal, including the length of the marriage, any antenuptial agreement, each spouse's needs and earning capability, and retirement benefits.
claims.quotedLanguage: 1. The community property must be assigned by the court in such proportions as the court, from all the facts of the case and the condition of the parties, deems just, with due consideration of the following factors: (a) Unless there are compelling reasons otherwise, there shall be a substantially equal division in value, considering debts, between the spouses. (b) Factors which may bear upon whether a division shall be equal, or the manner of division, include, but are not limited to: (1) Duration of the marriage;
claims.notes: ⚠️ NEVER write '50/50' or 'split equally' as a rule: the statute says 'substantially equal ... unless there are compelling reasons otherwise' and lists non-exclusive factors. Applies to COMMUNITY property; it does not divide separate property. Describe, never predict an outcome.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 32-712, a homestead selected from community property may be assigned to either spouse absolutely or for a limited period, or divided, or sold and the proceeds divided; a homestead selected from one spouse's separate property must be assigned to that former owner, subject to the court's power to assign it for a limited period to the other spouse.
claims.quotedLanguage: 2. If a homestead has been selected from the community property, it may be assigned to either party, either absolutely, provided such assignment is considered in distribution of the community property, or for a limited period, subject in the latter case to the future disposition of the court; or it may be divided or be sold and the proceeds divided. 3. If a homestead has been selected from the separate property of either, it must be assigned to the former owner of such property, subject to the power of the court to assign it for a limited period to the other spouse.
claims.notes: ⚠️ 'Homestead ... selected' is the statute's own term and predates the 1989 rewrite of Title 55 ch. 10 (automatic homestead, 55-1004). How the two interact was NOT researched — do not connect them in prose. Do not confuse with the creditor homestead exemption (55-1003) or the property-tax homeowner's exemption (63-602G).

claims.claim: Under Idaho Rule of Family Law Procedure 504(a)(2), a party may move for a temporary order to exclude a party from a residence, to divide community property or to order payment of debts and expenses, and the motion must state the specific relief requested, including the proposed division of property.
claims.quotedLanguage: A motion requesting a temporary order to exclude a party from a residence, to divide community property, or to order payment of debt and expenses, must state the specific relief requested, including the proposed division of property, the responsibility that each party would have to pay debts and expenses, and the income and assets that would be available to each party if the motion is granted.
claims.notes: ⚠️ A temporary order is something a party ASKS FOR by motion; it is not automatic. Say nothing about what any particular court has ordered or typically orders.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Rule of Family Law Procedure 506(e)(4), one ground on which a preliminary injunction may be granted in a family law case is that it appears by affidavit the responding party is about to remove or dispose of their property with intent to defraud the moving party.
claims.quotedLanguage: (e) Grounds for Preliminary Injunction. A preliminary injunction may be granted in the following cases: ... (4) when it appears, by affidavit, that the responding party is about to remove or to dispose of the responding party’s property with intent to defraud the moving party or;
claims.notes: ⚠️ The trailing 'or;' is verbatim from the court's page. Rule 506 also lists other grounds (e)(1)-(3),(5); (4) is the one that names disposing of property. ⚠️ NEGATIVE FINDING, NOT A CLAIM: a search of the full IRFLP text cached 2026-11-12 found no automatic restraining order on transferring property upon filing. Do not state 'Idaho has no automatic restraining order' as fact — local orders, standing orders or a specific court's practice were not checked.

claims.claim: Idaho Rule of Family Law Procedure 401(f) requires each party in a contested family law action, unless the parties have a written agreement disposing of all property issues or no property is at issue, to list real and personal property worth more than $100 with an estimated current fair market value, and to give the other party copies of all deeds, deeds of trust, purchase agreements, escrow documents and settlement sheets for real property owned by any party.
claims.quotedLanguage: (f) Property. Unless the parties have entered into a written agreement disposing of all property issues in the case or no property is at issue in the case, each party will prepare a list of all items having a fair market value more than $100 of real and personal property, ... (1) all deeds, deeds of trust, purchase agreements, escrow documents, settlement sheets, and all other documents that disclose the ownership, legal description, purchase price, and encumbrances of all real property owned by any party;
claims.notes: Rule 401 is titled 'Mandatory Disclosure in Contested Proceedings'; 401(a) sets the deadline at 35 days after a responsive pleading (not used in prose; if used, quote 401(a) separately). ⚠️ This is DISCOVERY between spouses — never confuse with the seller property condition disclosure to a buyer (55-2504).

claims.claim: In Idaho a money judgment becomes a lien on the debtor's real property in a county only when a transcript or abstract of it is recorded with that county's recorder — from the time of recording, and not before — and the lien then reaches non-exempt real property the debtor owns in that county at the time or acquires before the lien expires.
claims.quotedLanguage: may be recorded with the recorder of any county of this state, who shall immediately record and docket the same as by law provided, and from the time of such recording, and not before, the judgment so recorded becomes a lien upon all real property of the judgment debtor in the county, not exempt from execution, owned by him at the time or acquired afterwards at any time prior to the expiration of the lien
claims.notes: ⚠️ COUNTY-BY-COUNTY. The lien attaches only in the county where the abstract is recorded. A judgment entered in court but not recorded in Ada County is not a lien on Ada County real property under this section — but the debt itself still exists. Never write 'a judgment automatically attaches to your house'. ⚠️ 'not exempt from execution' interacts with the homestead exemption (55-1003, claim id-homestead-creditor-175k); how they interact on a voluntary sale is NOT stated here — send readers to an attorney.

claims.claim: Apart from child-support and recorded crime-victim restitution judgments, the lien from a recorded Idaho judgment continues ten years from the date of the judgment, unless the judgment is satisfied sooner or enforcement is stayed on appeal.
claims.quotedLanguage: The lien resulting from recording of a judgment other than for support of a child or for restitution owed to a crime victim where the order of restitution has been recorded as a judgment pursuant to section 19-5305 , Idaho Code, continues ten (10) years from the date of the judgment, unless the judgment be previously satisfied, or unless the enforcement of the judgment be stayed upon an appeal as provided by law.
claims.notes: ⚠️ Ten years runs from the DATE OF THE JUDGMENT, not from the date of recording. Must be stated with the renewal rule (ln-judgment-renewal-order) — a lien can be extended, so 'it expires after ten years' alone is wrong. Restitution judgments run 20 years (ln-judgment-lien-restitution-twenty-years); child support runs differently (ln-judgment-lien-child-support).

claims.claim: Before an Idaho judgment lien (or any renewal of it) expires, and unless the judgment has been satisfied, the court that entered the judgment may on motion enter an order renewing it; once recorded like the original, the lien continues ten years from the date of the renewal order, keeping the original judgment's date and priority.
claims.quotedLanguage: Unless the judgment has been satisfied, at any time prior to the expiration of the lien created by section 10-1110 , Idaho Code, or any renewal thereof, the court that entered the judgment, other than a judgment for child support, may, upon motion, renew such judgment by entry of an order renewing judgment. The order renewing judgment may be recorded in the same manner as the original judgment, and the lien established or continued thereby shall continue for ten (10) years from the date of the order renewing judgment. Entry of an order renewing judgment maintains both the date of the original judgment and the priority of collection thereof
claims.notes: ⚠️ 'or any renewal thereof' — renewal can repeat. Subsection (2) separately allows renewal of child-support judgments. Renewal is discretionary ('may') and must be sought BEFORE expiry. Do not tell a reader an old judgment 'has expired' — whether it was renewed is a records question.

claims.claim: A recorded Idaho divorce or separate-maintenance decree providing for periodic child support or alimony is a lien only for payments that are delinquent or not made when due; a lien arising from a delinquency under an Idaho child-support judgment continues until ten years after the death or emancipation of the last child owed support, unless renewed, satisfied or stayed on appeal.
claims.quotedLanguage: such judgment or decree shall be a lien only in an amount for payments so provided, delinquent or not made when due ... A lien arising from the delinquency of a payment due under a judgment for support of a child issued by an Idaho court continues until ten (10) years after the death or emancipation of the last child for whom support is owed under the judgment unless the underlying judgment is renewed, is previously satisfied or the enforcement of the judgment is stayed upon an appeal as provided by law.
claims.notes: The lien amount is limited to DELINQUENT payments, not the whole future obligation. Separate from the Department of Health and Welfare lien under 7-1206 (ln-child-support-department-lien), which is perfected with the Secretary of State, not the county recorder.

claims.claim: A lien from an Idaho crime-victim restitution order recorded as a judgment under Idaho Code 19-5305 continues twenty years from the date of the judgment, unless satisfied sooner or stayed or set aside.
claims.quotedLanguage: A lien arising from an order for restitution to a crime victim where the order of restitution has been recorded as a judgment pursuant to section 19-5305 , Idaho Code, continues until twenty (20) years from the date of the judgment, unless the judgment be previously satisfied, or unless the judgment is stayed or set aside.
claims.notes: Niche; mentioned only so the ten-year rule is not stated as universal.

claims.claim: Where Idaho's Department of Health and Welfare is or has been providing child-support enforcement services, a delinquency under a child-support order creates a lien that arises on and attaches to the obligor's real and personal property; once it equals at least 90 days of support or $2,000, whichever is less, it may be perfected by filing with the Idaho Secretary of State, and a perfected lien is automatically released when the delinquency reaches a zero balance.
claims.quotedLanguage: Upon a delinquency under a child support order for which the department is or has been providing child support enforcement services, a lien arises upon and attaches to the real and personal property of an obligor. When the amount of the lien is equal to or greater than the total support owing for at least ninety (90) days, or two thousand dollars ($2,000), whichever is less, the lien may be perfected by a filing with the office of the secretary of state. A perfected lien shall include all subsequently arising delinquencies. When a lien has been perfected pursuant to this section and the underlying delinquency reaches a zero balance or is otherwise satisfied, the lien is automatically released. ... "Department" means the department of health and welfare.
claims.notes: ⚠️ Applies ONLY to cases where the Department provides enforcement services. ⚠️ Filed with the SECRETARY OF STATE, not the county recorder — a county-records search will not necessarily show it. Amended 2025 (ch. 201). 'Department' = the Idaho Department of Health and Welfare per 7-1202(3). Subsection (3): no enforcement until 10 days after certified-mail notice to the obligor.

claims.claim: Under Idaho's mechanics' and materialmen's lien law, every person who performs labor on, or furnishes materials for, the construction, alteration or repair of a building or other structure — and licensed engineers and surveyors under contract for professional services on a land or building improvement — has a lien on that property, whether the work was ordered by the owner or the owner's agent; contractors and subcontractors in charge of the work are treated as the owner's agent for this purpose.
claims.quotedLanguage: Every person performing labor upon, or furnishing materials to be used in the construction, alteration or repair of any mining claim, building, wharf, bridge, ditch, dike, flume, tunnel, fence, machinery, railroad, wagon road, aqueduct to create hydraulic power, or any other structure ... has a lien upon the same for the work or labor done or professional services or materials furnished, whether done or furnished at the instance of the owner of the building or other improvement or his agent; and every contractor, subcontractor, architect, builder or any person having charge of any mining claim, or of the construction, alteration or repair, either in whole or in part, of any building or other improvement, as aforesaid, shall be held to be the agent of the owner for the purpose of this chapter
claims.notes: ⚠️ The 'agent of the owner' clause means a SUBCONTRACTOR or SUPPLIER the homeowner never hired can claim a lien. Do not state whether a homeowner who already paid the general contractor is protected — the statute here does not say, and that is a classic attorney question.

claims.claim: An Idaho mechanic's lien claimant must file the claim for record with the recorder of the county where the property sits within 90 days after completing the labor or services or furnishing the materials, verified by oath, and must serve a copy on the owner or reputed owner, personally or by certified mail, no later than five business days after filing.
claims.quotedLanguage: Any person claiming a lien pursuant to the provisions of this chapter must file a claim for record with the county recorder for the county in which such property or some part thereof is situated. (2) The claim shall be filed within ninety (90) days after the completion of the labor or services, or furnishing of materials. ... Such delivery or mailing shall be made no later than five (5) business days following the filing of said claim of lien.
claims.notes: ⚠️ 90 days runs from COMPLETION of that claimant's work or materials, not from the start of the job or the invoice date. Subsection (7): prevailing party in a court proceeding on the lien recovers reasonable attorney's fees and costs — not used in prose. Do not say whether a particular lien was timely.

claims.claim: An Idaho mechanic's lien binds the property for no longer than six months after the claim is filed unless proceedings to enforce it are commenced in a proper court within that time, or unless a payment on account or an extension of credit is endorsed on the record of the lien (in which case six months after that payment or the extension's expiry); the lien of a final judgment obtained on such a lien ceases ten years after the judgment becomes final.
claims.quotedLanguage: No lien provided for in this chapter binds any building, mining claim, improvement or structure for a longer period than six (6) months after the claim has been filed, unless proceedings be commenced in a proper court within that time to enforce such lien; or unless a payment on account is made, or extension of credit given with expiration date thereof, and such payment or credit and expiration date, is endorsed on the record of the lien, then six (6) months after the date of such payment or expiration of extension. The lien of a final judgment obtained on any lien provided for in this chapter shall cease ten (10) years from the date the judgment becomes final.
claims.notes: ⚠️ A lapsed claim may still SIT ON THE RECORD — the statute says it no longer binds the property, not that it disappears from the county index. Whether a given recorded claim is still enforceable (was suit filed?) is a court-records and attorney question. Never tell a reader their lien 'has expired'.

claims.claim: Idaho mechanics' liens share equal footing within their class regardless of filing date, and are preferred to any lien, mortgage or other encumbrance that attached after the building or improvement was commenced or work or materials began, and to any unrecorded encumbrance of which the lienholder had no notice at that time.
claims.quotedLanguage: The liens provided for in this chapter shall be on equal footing with those liens within the same class of liens, without reference to the date of the filing of the lien claim or claims and are preferred to any lien, mortgage or other encumbrance, which may have attached subsequent to the time when the building, improvement or structure was commenced, work done, equipment, materials or fixtures were rented or leased, or materials or professional services were commenced to be furnished
claims.notes: ⚠️ Priority relates back to when the WORK STARTED, not to when the claim was filed. Describe only; do not rank liens on a reader's property.

claims.claim: Idaho allows a mechanic's lien of record on real property to be released by posting a surety bond under Idaho Code 45-519 through 45-524; the statutory bond form is in one and a half times the amount of the claim, from which the surety pays what a court adjudges was secured by the lien, with interest, costs and attorney's fees.
claims.quotedLanguage: A mechanic's lien of record upon real property may be released upon the posting of a surety bond in the manner provided in sections 45-519 through 45-524 , Idaho Code. ... (1-1/2 x claim), from which sum they will pay the claimant such amount as a court of competent jurisdiction may adjudge to have been secured by his lien, with interest, costs and attorney's fees.
claims.notes: The 1.5x figure appears in the STATUTORY BOND FORM in 45-519, not in operative prose; state it as 'the statutory bond form is written for one and a half times the claim'. Bond must be executed by a corporation authorized to do surety business in Idaho. Sections 45-520 to 45-524 (procedure) were NOT read — do not describe the procedure beyond this.

claims.claim: Idaho's Homeowner's Association Act defines a homeowner's association as an incorporated or unincorporated residential association whose membership is based on owning or possessing an interest in real property and which has authority, under recorded covenants, bylaws or other governing documents, to assess and record liens against its members' real property.
claims.quotedLanguage: "Homeowner's association" means any incorporated or unincorporated residential association: (i) In which membership is based on owning or possessing an interest in real property; and (ii) That has the authority, pursuant to recorded covenants, bylaws, or other governing documents, to assess and record liens against the real property of its members.
claims.notes: Lien AUTHORITY flows from the recorded governing documents; the Act's definition presupposes it. Amended 2026 (ch. 251) — current text read 2026-11-12.

claims.claim: An Idaho homeowner's association may levy an assessment against a lot for the reasonable costs of maintaining common areas it owns and maintains; to claim a lien for it, the association must file a verified claim in the county where the lot sits stating the amount due, and within five business days of recording must serve a copy on the owner by personal delivery or certified mail; once recorded, the claim automatically accumulates later unpaid assessments.
claims.quotedLanguage: A homeowner's association may levy an assessment against a lot for the reasonable costs incurred in the maintenance of common areas consisting of real property owned and maintained by the homeowner's association. (2)(a) A homeowner's association claiming a lien under subsection (1) of this section must file a claim in the county in which the lot or some part thereof is located. ... such claim shall automatically accumulate the subsequent unpaid assessments without the necessity of further filings under this section. ... Within five (5) business days after recording a lien on the property, the homeowner's association shall serve, by personal delivery to the owner or reputed owner or by certified mail to the last known address of the owner or reputed owner, a true and correct copy of the recorded lien.
claims.notes: ⚠️ The lien in 55-3207(1) is tied to assessments for COMMON-AREA MAINTENANCE. The section does not say fines are lienable — do not claim either way. Condominiums are under a different act (55-1518, ln-condo-assessment-lien-one-year). No duration/expiry is stated in 55-3207 — do not invent one.

claims.claim: An Idaho homeowner's association lien may be enforced by the board on the association's behalf; the association may also sue for a money judgment for unpaid assessments without foreclosing or waiving the lien, or take a deed in lieu of foreclosure, and recovery in such an action satisfies the lien to that extent.
claims.quotedLanguage: The lien may be enforced by the board acting on behalf of the homeowner's association. (4) This section does not prohibit a homeowner's association from pursuing an action to recover sums for which subsection (1) of this section creates a lien or from taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure in satisfaction of the lien. (5) An action to recover a money judgment for unpaid assessments may be maintained without foreclosing or waiving the lien securing the claim for unpaid assessments. However, recovery on the action operates to satisfy the lien, or the portion thereof, for which recovery is made.
claims.notes: Describe only. The section does not set out a foreclosure procedure or timeline.

claims.claim: An Idaho homeowner's association must give a member, or the member's agent, a free statement of the member's assessment account within five business days of a written request, listing all outstanding assessments, charges and fees including any transfer fee, late fees and interest; the association is bound by the amounts in the statement, and charging for it violates the Idaho Consumer Protection Act.
claims.quotedLanguage: A homeowner's association or its agent shall provide a member and the member's agent, if any, a statement of the member's assessment account no more than five (5) business days after a written request by the member or the member's agent is received by the manager, president, board member, or other agent of the homeowner's association, or any combination thereof. The homeowner's association will be bound by the amounts set forth within the statement of assessment account. The statement of assessment account shall include all outstanding assessments, charges, and fees, including any transfer fee, that are due and owing to the homeowner's association, including any late fees or interest that may have accrued. ... No fee shall be charged by a homeowner's association or its agent for providing a statement of the member's assessment account.
claims.notes: Five BUSINESS days, after the WRITTEN request is RECEIVED. The 'bound by' sentence is the useful one for a seller. Amended 2023, 2024, 2025. Subsection (2): transfer fee only if the CC&Rs expressly authorize it — not used in prose.

claims.claim: Under Idaho's Condominium Property Act, a condominium assessment and authorized charges become a lien when the management body records a notice of assessment with the county recorder; unless satisfied and released or enforcement is begun, the lien expires one year after the notice is recorded, extendable by the management body for no more than one additional year by recording a written extension.
claims.quotedLanguage: shall be and become a lien upon the condominium assessed when the management body causes to be recorded with the county recorder of the county in which such condominium is located a notice of assessment ... Unless sooner satisfied and released or the enforcement thereof initiated as hereafter provided such lien shall expire and be of no further force or effect one (1) year from the date of recordation of said notice of assessment; provided, however, that said one-year period may be extended by the management body for not to exceed one (1) additional year by recording a written extension thereof.
claims.notes: ⚠️ CONDOMINIUMS ONLY. Whether a given association falls under 55-1518, the HOA Act (55-3207), or both is a question for an attorney; do not assign a reader's community to one. The section also says the lien may be enforced by sale in the manner for powers of sale in deeds of trust.

claims.claim: Idaho property taxes levied on real property are a first and prior lien on the assessed property, discharged only by payment or cancellation of the taxes as the tax title provides, and property tax liens are perpetual and continuous.
claims.quotedLanguage: All property taxes levied upon real property shall be a first and prior lien upon the real property assessed therefor, and shall only be discharged by the payment or cancellation of the property taxes as provided in this title. ... Property tax liens shall be perpetual and continuous on all personal, operating and real property.
claims.notes: ⚠️ 'First and prior' — property taxes outrank the other liens on this page. 'Perpetual' means there is no expiry clock comparable to judgment or mechanic's liens. Pair with the existing tax-deed claims (id-tax-deed-three-year-delinquency, id-tax-deed-redemption-fourteen-months) for what happens on delinquency. The Jan 1 lien date is in ada-assessment-market-value-jan-1.

claims.claim: The IRS describes a federal tax lien as the government's legal claim against a taxpayer's property — including real estate — when a tax debt is not paid; it exists after the IRS assesses the liability, sends a Notice and Demand for Payment, and the taxpayer neglects or refuses to pay in time, and the IRS may file a public Notice of Federal Tax Lien to alert creditors.
claims.quotedLanguage: A federal tax lien is the government's legal claim against your property when you neglect or fail to pay a tax debt. The lien protects the government's interest in all your property, including real estate, personal property and financial assets. ... The IRS files a public document, the Notice of Federal Tax Lien , to alert creditors that the government has a legal right to your property.
claims.notes: IRS explanatory web page, not the Internal Revenue Code itself (26 USC 6321-6325 were not read). The page also says the lien attaches to future assets acquired during the lien's duration.

claims.claim: The IRS says paying the tax debt in full is the best way to get rid of a federal tax lien, and that it releases the lien within 30 days after the debt is paid.
claims.quotedLanguage: Paying your tax debt - in full - is the best way to get rid of a federal tax lien. The IRS releases your lien within 30 days after you have paid your tax debt.
claims.notes: 30 days is the IRS's stated practice on its own page. Do not convert it into a closing-timeline promise.

claims.claim: The IRS distinguishes three tools: a discharge removes the federal tax lien from specific property; a subordination does not remove the lien but lets other creditors move ahead of the IRS; and a withdrawal removes the public Notice of Federal Tax Lien while the taxpayer remains liable for the amount due.
claims.quotedLanguage: A "discharge" removes the lien from specific property. ... "Subordination" does not remove the lien but allows other creditors to move ahead of the IRS, which may make it easier to get a loan or mortgage. ... A "withdrawal" removes the public Notice of Federal Tax Lien and assures that the IRS is not competing with other creditors for your property; however, you are still liable for the amount due.
claims.notes: ⚠️ Withdrawal ≠ debt forgiven. Subordination is a refinancing tool, not a sale tool. Eligibility is in Pub 783 / Pub 784 / Form 12277 — do not state that anyone qualifies.

claims.claim: IRS Publication 783 says a Certificate of Discharge under Internal Revenue Code section 6325(b) removes the United States' lien from the property named in the certificate, that the application is made on Form 14135, and that it should be submitted at least 45 days before the transaction date on which the certificate is needed.
claims.quotedLanguage: 6325(b) removes the United States' lien from the property ... Complete Form 14135, Application for Certificate ... Please submit your application at least 45 days before the ... transaction date that the certificate of discharge is needed.
claims.notes: ⚠️ VERIFIER NOTE: pdftotext -layout interleaves Pub 783's two columns, so contiguous sentences are split across lines in the extracted text; the '...' joins here bridge column breaks, not omitted words (except between the three sentences). Pub 783 Rev. 12-2022. 45 days is the IRS's request, not a guaranteed processing time.

claims.claim: IRS Publication 783 describes, among other bases, a discharge under section 6325(b)(2)(A) when the liability is partly paid with an amount not less than the value of the United States' interest in the property being discharged, and under section 6325(b)(2)(B) when the government's interest has no value because debts senior to the federal tax lien exceed the property's fair market value or sale value.
claims.quotedLanguage: provision when the tax liability is partially satisfied with an ... amount paid that is not less than the value of the United ... States' interest in the property being discharged. ... provision when it is determined that the government's ... interest in the property has no value. The debts senior to ... the federal tax lien are greater than the fair market value of ... the property or greater than the sale value of the property.
claims.notes: ⚠️ Same column-interleave caveat as ln-irs-discharge-apply-45-days. Pub 783 also requires an appraisal by a disinterested third party and lists other bases (6325(b)(1), (b)(3), (b)(4)). Never say a reader's lien 'has no value' or that the IRS will accept a figure — the IRS decides.

claims.claim: IRS Publication 784 says a Certificate of Subordination under Internal Revenue Code section 6325(d)(1) and (d)(2) allows a named creditor to move its junior position ahead of the United States' position for the property named in the certificate.
claims.quotedLanguage: Section 6325(d)(1) and 6325(d)(2) allows a named creditor to ... move their junior creditor position ahead of the United States' ... position for the property named in the certificate.
claims.notes: Same column-interleave caveat. Subordination is about letting a lender go first — typically a refinance, not a sale; included so readers do not confuse it with discharge.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 15-3-201, the first probate or appointment proceeding after a death is venued in the county where the decedent was domiciled at death; for a decedent not domiciled in Idaho, in any county where the decedent's property was located.
claims.quotedLanguage: (a) Venue for the first informal or formal testacy or appointment proceedings after a decedent's death is: (1) In the county where the decedent had his domicile at the time of his death; or (2) If the decedent was not domiciled in this state, in any county where property of the decedent was located at the time of his death.
claims.notes: Venue turns on DOMICILE, not on where the house is. A house in Ada County owned by someone who lived in Canyon County is probated in Canyon. Never say 'probate is filed where the property is' except for a non-Idaho domiciliary. claims.claim: A formal testacy proceeding in Idaho is litigation to determine whether the decedent left a valid will. Once a previously appointed personal representative receives notice of one, they must refrain from further distribution while it is pending; a petitioner may ask the court to restrain the acting representative's powers, but absent such an order the proceeding affects only powers relating to distribution.

A petitioner who seeks the appointment of a different personal representative in a formal proceeding also may request an order restraining the acting personal representative from exercising any of the powers of his office and requesting the appointment of a special administrator. In the absence of a request, or if the request is denied, the commencement of a formal proceeding has no effect on the powers and duties of a previously appointed personal representative other than those relating to distribution.
claims.notes: Do not say a will contest 'freezes' a sale. The statute freezes DISTRIBUTION; other powers continue unless a restraining order is sought and granted. Whether a given sale is wise during a contest is for the estate's attorney. claims.claim: Idaho sets a priority order for appointment as personal representative: the person with priority under a probated will; a surviving spouse who is a devisee; other devisees; the surviving spouse; other heirs; then, 45 days after death, any creditor; and if a petition has been filed and 60 days pass with no proper person consenting to act, the public administrator. Persons sharing a priority who do not renounce must concur in nominating someone or in applying.
claims.quotedLanguage: (a) Whether the proceedings are formal or informal, persons who are not disqualified have priority for appointment in the following order: (1) the person with priority as determined by a probated will including a person nominated by a power conferred in a will; (2) the surviving spouse of the decedent who is a devisee of the decedent; (3) other devisees of the decedent; (4) the surviving spouse of the decedent; (5) other heirs of the decedent; (6) forty-five (45) days after the death of the decedent, any creditor; (7) if a petition for appointment of a personal representative has been filed and sixty (60) days have elapsed during which no consent to act has been filed by any proper person, the public administrator shall act as personal representative unless and until a proper person consents to act. ... When two (2) or more persons share a priority, those of them who do not renounce must concur in nominating another to act for them, or in applying for appointment.
claims.notes: Pairs with ada-treasurer-ex-officio-public-administrator (the Ada Treasurer is the public administrator).
